CruiseMapper currently has no ship schedule for Port Alcoutim (Portugal)

Alcoutim is a Douro River cruise port and town in southeastern Portugal, with population around 3,000. The town is located close to the border with Spain.

Alcoutim municipality lies in the northeast corner of Faro District. It is Portugal's least densely populated municipality, limited on the east by Huelva Province (Spain), on the north by Mertola Municipality, on the southwest by Tavira Municipality, on the southeast by Castro Marim Municipality, and on the west by Loule and Almodovar Municipality.

The municipality's administrative center is Alcoutim, which is located at the extreme eastern part on the Spanish frontier, across Guadiana River from the town of Sanlucar de Guadiana, Huelva Province in Spain.

The municipal holiday date is June 13.

Moorish Alcoutim Castle dates back to the 14th century.

Administratively, the municipality of Alcoutim is divided into four civil parishes, including: Alcoutim e Pereiro, Gioes, Martim Longo and Vaqueiros.

Alcoutim is a small river-cruise stop on the Guadiana, directly opposite Sanlúcar de Guadiana in Spain. The historic center is compact and best explored on foot. Once ashore, independent sightseeing is straightforward, although several streets and the approaches to the castle are uphill.

Independent sightseeing: Independent with some planning. The town itself is easy to explore without a tour, but passengers should confirm the ship's exact landing arrangements because of current restrictions on the river pier.

Getting from the Cruise Port

Alcoutim does not have a conventional ocean-cruise terminal. River cruise vessels normally approach the town via the Guadiana, with the riverfront immediately beside the historic center.

Important access note: in February 2026, the port authority closed Cais de Alcoutim and several other Guadiana piers after flood damage, prohibiting vessel use until safety assessments and repairs are completed. Passengers on a scheduled Alcoutim call should therefore follow the cruise operator's current instructions regarding the actual landing point, tender or any alternative transfer.

Once passengers reach central Alcoutim, almost everything of interest is within walking distance. A taxi is unnecessary for the main sights.

Best Ways to Spend Your Time

Explore Alcoutim Castle and the Riverside Center

Allow about 1.5–2.5 hours for the essential sights. Walk along the Guadiana waterfront, see the old quay area and Igreja Matriz, then climb through the whitewashed streets to Alcoutim Castle. The castle walls provide broad views across the river to Spain and contain an archaeological museum when open.

This is the most practical choice for a short call and requires no organized excursion. The town is compact, although the climb to the castle involves slopes and some uneven surfaces.

Walk to Pego Fundo River Beach

Praia Fluvial do Pego Fundo is approximately 0.5 km (0.3 mi) from the center. It has a sandy bathing area on the Ribeira de Cadavais and is a realistic addition to a town visit, particularly in warm weather.

Allow 1–2 hours if you want time for a swim or rest. Beach facilities and lifeguard coverage are seasonal, so do not assume full services outside the summer bathing period.

Cross to Sanlúcar de Guadiana

The Spanish village of Sanlúcar de Guadiana sits directly opposite Alcoutim. Small passenger boats have traditionally provided the short cross-river connection, making it possible to visit two countries during one stop.

Because river-pier conditions and private boat operations can change, only attempt the crossing if the service is confirmed on the day. Allow around 1.5–2 hours for the crossing and a short walk around Sanlúcar, and return to the Portuguese side well before the ship's all-aboard time.

Take a Guadiana Boat Trip

Local operators traditionally offer short river trips as well as longer outings toward nearby Guadiana villages. A short cruise can complement a walking visit, but availability depends on river conditions and usable landing facilities.

For cruise passengers, a short prearranged trip is more practical than a half-day journey. Do not make an independent boat excursion the centerpiece of a tight call unless both departure and return arrangements are confirmed.

Self-Guided Walking Tour

Alcoutim Heritage and River Walk

Distance: about 4 km (2.5 mi). Pure walking time: approximately 1–1.5 hours. Recommended total time: 2.5–3 hours with sightseeing. Difficulty: Moderate, with hills and some uneven surfaces.

  1. Praça da República: Begin in the small central square after reaching the town center.
  2. Guadiana waterfront and Cais Velho: Follow the riverside promenade for views across to Sanlúcar de Guadiana.
  3. Igreja Matriz de São Salvador: See the parish church beside the old waterfront area.
  4. Alcoutim Castle: Climb to the medieval fortress for the principal viewpoint over the town and river.
  5. Ermida de Nossa Senhora da Conceição: Continue uphill to this small historic church and another elevated viewpoint.
  6. Praia Fluvial do Pego Fundo: Descend toward the river beach, approximately 0.5 km (0.3 mi) from the center.
  7. Castelo Velho area: Continue on the hillier part of the route toward the archaeological remains if time and weather permit.
  8. Return to central Alcoutim: Complete the loop back toward Praça da República and the ship's designated embarkation point.

The municipality's full local walking route is hilly, reaching elevations of roughly 140 m (460 ft). Passengers who prefer an easier walk can omit Castelo Velho and simply return from Pego Fundo to the waterfront.

Practical Tips

  • Alcoutim is better treated as a compact destination in its own right rather than as a gateway for a long road excursion elsewhere in the Algarve.
  • Summer conditions can be very hot, and several sightseeing streets are exposed and uphill. Carry water and use suitable footwear.
  • Check the castle and museum opening times on the day rather than planning the entire visit around an interior visit.
  • If crossing to Spain or taking an independent river trip, build in at least an hour of additional return margin rather than relying on the final available boat.
  • Current river-pier restrictions make the cruise operator's landing and re-embarkation instructions particularly important.
